question: Count the customers whose country is France. Return exactly one column: the customer count.
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE country = 'France';

question: List all products in the Electronics category. Return exactly one column: the product name. No particular row order is required.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics';

question: Count the orders placed from January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025, inclusive. Return exactly one column: the order count.
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01';

question: For each product with at least one order, calculate the total quantity sold across all its orders. Treat each product ID as a separate product. Return exactly two columns, in this order: product name, total quantity sold. No particular row order is required.
expected_sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(o.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name;

question: Find the single customer who placed the most orders, counting each orders row as one order. Treat each customer ID as a separate customer. If customers tie, choose the customer with the smallest customer ID. Return exactly two columns, in this order: customer name, number of orders.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.id ASC LIMIT 1;

question: For each product with at least one order, calculate its total revenue across all its orders, using product price multiplied by order quantity. Treat each product ID as a separate product. Return exactly two columns, in this order: product name, total revenue. Do not round the revenue. No particular row order is required.
expected_sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name;

question: Find the single customer with the highest total spending across all their orders, using product price multiplied by order quantity. Treat each customer ID as a separate customer. If customers tie, choose the customer with the smallest customer ID. Return exactly two columns, in this order: customer name, total spending. Do not round the spending.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.id ASC LIMIT 1;

question: Find the single product category with the highest total revenue across all orders, using product price multiplied by order quantity. If categories tie, choose the category whose name comes first in ascending alphabetical order. Return exactly two columns, in this order: category name, total revenue. Do not round the revenue.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC, p.category ASC LIMIT 1;

question: Calculate each customer's total spending across all their orders, using product price multiplied by order quantity. Treat each customer ID as a separate customer. Among customers with at least one order, find those whose total spending is strictly greater than the average of these customer totals. Exclude customers with no orders from the average. Return exactly two columns, in this order: customer name, total spending. Do not round the spending. No particular row order is required.
expected_sql: WITH customer_spending AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name) SELECT name, total_spent FROM customer_spending WHERE total_spent > (SELECT AVG(total_spent) FROM customer_spending);

question: Find the single product ordered by the largest number of distinct customers, identifying products by product ID and customers by customer ID. Count a customer only once per product, even if they ordered it multiple times. If products tie, choose the product with the smallest product ID. Return exactly two columns, in this order: product name, distinct customer count.
expected_sql: SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY customer_count DESC, p.id ASC LIMIT 1;

question: How many customers live in Tunisia?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE country = 'Tunisia';

question: List the names of customers from Italy.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE country = 'Italy';

question: Which products belong to the Sports category? Show their names and prices, in that order.
expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE category = 'Sports';

question: Show the names and prices of products costing less than 50, with the name first.
expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price < 50;

question: How many products cost at least 100?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price >= 100;

question: What is the average price of a Furniture product?
expected_sql: SELECT AVG(price) FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture';

question: Give the lowest product price in the catalog.
expected_sql: SELECT MIN(price) FROM products;

question: What is the highest price among Clothing products?
expected_sql: SELECT MAX(price) FROM products WHERE category = 'Clothing';

question: How many orders were placed during February 2024, including February 29?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2024-02-01' AND order_date < '2024-03-01';

question: List order IDs and dates for purchases made from June 1 through June 30, 2025, inclusive, with the ID first.
expected_sql: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-06-01' AND order_date <= '2025-06-30';

question: What is the total quantity across orders placed in 2024?
expected_sql: SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date < '2025-01-01';

question: How many orders have a quantity of at least four?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE quantity >= 4;

question: Show each different customer country once, in alphabetical order.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers ORDER BY country ASC;

question: Find the three cheapest products. Display product ID, name, and price, ordered from lowest price to highest, with smaller product IDs first when prices tie.
expected_sql: SELECT id, name, price FROM products ORDER BY price ASC, id ASC LIMIT 3;

question: Which product has the highest price? If prices tie, choose the smallest product ID. Show its name followed by its price.
expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC, id ASC LIMIT 1;

question: On what date was the earliest order placed? Show only the date.
expected_sql: SELECT MIN(order_date) FROM orders;

question: List the names of products priced from 50 to 100, including both endpoints.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price >= 50 AND price <= 100;

question: How many customers are from either Germany or Spain?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE country IN ('Germany', 'Spain');

question: What is the average quantity per order?
expected_sql: SELECT AVG(quantity) FROM orders;

question: Show the five most recent orders as order ID followed by order date. Sort newest dates first, and smaller order IDs first for orders on the same date.
expected_sql: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders ORDER BY order_date DESC, id ASC LIMIT 5;

question: For orders placed by customers from Tunisia, list the order ID, customer name, and order date, in that order.
expected_sql: SELECT o.id, c.name, o.order_date FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.country = 'Tunisia';

question: Show the order ID, product name, and quantity for orders of Furniture products, in that order.
expected_sql: SELECT o.id, p.name, o.quantity FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE p.category = 'Furniture';

question: Which customers have ordered the product named Laptop? List each customer once by customer ID followed by name.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE p.name = 'Laptop';

question: For every customer, including those with no orders, show customer ID, name, and number of orders. Customers without orders should have a count of zero.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

question: For each product sold in 2025, report its product ID, name, and total quantity sold during that year.
expected_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, SUM(o.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY p.id, p.name;

question: How many customers are registered in each country? Show country followed by customer count.
expected_sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country;

question: What is the average catalog price in each product category? Display category followed by average price.
expected_sql: SELECT category, AVG(price) AS average_price FROM products GROUP BY category;

question: For each country whose customers have placed orders, show the country and its total number of orders.
expected_sql: SELECT c.country, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country;

question: How many distinct customers have purchased an Electronics product? Count each customer ID once, even if they made several purchases.
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics';

question: Which customers placed at least six orders? Display customer ID, name, and order count.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 6;

question: Identify products with more than 150 units sold across all orders. Show product ID, product name, and total units sold.
expected_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, SUM(o.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING SUM(o.quantity) > 150;

question: What revenue came from orders placed in 2024? Revenue is product price multiplied by quantity, totaled across those orders. Show only the total revenue without rounding.
expected_sql: SELECT SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-01-01';

question: Report revenue for each product category with orders in 2025. Revenue is product price multiplied by quantity. Show category followed by total revenue for that year, without rounding.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY p.category;

question: Which five customers placed the most orders in 2024? Show customer ID, name, and order count for customers with orders that year, sorted by count from highest to lowest and then by customer ID from smallest to largest.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.id ASC LIMIT 5;

question: Among products with at least one order, which has the smallest total quantity sold? Break ties using the smallest product ID. Give product ID, name, and total quantity sold.
expected_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, SUM(o.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY total_quantity ASC, p.id ASC LIMIT 1;

question: For each month of 2025 that contains orders, show the month as YYYY-MM followed by its order count. List months from earliest to latest.
expected_sql: SELECT substr(order_date, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY substr(order_date, 1, 7) ORDER BY month ASC;

question: For each customer who has ordered, show customer ID, name, and the date of their most recent order.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

question: Which countries have at least 50 registered customers? Give the country and customer count.
expected_sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50;

question: List customers who have never placed an order, showing customer ID followed by name.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL;

question: For each product category purchased by customers from France, show the category and total quantity those customers ordered.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE c.country = 'France' GROUP BY p.category;

question: For each country with orders, how many distinct customers placed orders during 2025? Show country followed by that customer count, omitting countries with no orders in that year.
expected_sql: SELECT c.country, COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY c.country;

question: Which products were ordered at least once from July 1 through December 31, 2024, inclusive? List each product once as product ID followed by name.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.name FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2024-07-01' AND o.order_date <= '2024-12-31';

question: Among customers who ordered in 2025, which spent more that year than the average total spending of those customers? Spending is product price multiplied by quantity. Show customer ID, name, and total spending in 2025 without rounding.
expected_sql: WITH spending AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY c.id, c.name) SELECT id, name, total_spent FROM spending WHERE total_spent > (SELECT AVG(total_spent) FROM spending);

question: Which products cost more than the average catalog price within their own category? Show product ID, name, category, and price, in that order.
expected_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, p.category, p.price FROM products p WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(p2.price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category = p.category);

question: Which country generated the most revenue from orders in 2024? Attribute each order to its customer country and calculate revenue as product price multiplied by quantity. For equal totals, choose the country first alphabetically. Show country followed by total revenue without rounding.
expected_sql: SELECT c.country, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.country ASC LIMIT 1;

question: Among customers from Germany who have ordered, who has the highest total spending across all orders? Spending is product price multiplied by quantity. Break ties with the smallest customer ID. Show customer ID, name, and total spending without rounding.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(p.price * o.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE c.country = 'Germany' GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.id ASC LIMIT 1;

question: Which product reached the most distinct customers during 2025? Count each customer ID once per product and consider only products ordered that year. If counts tie, select the smallest product ID. Show product ID, name, and distinct customer count.
expected_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM products p JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY customer_count DESC, p.id ASC LIMIT 1;

question: Identify customers who bought at least one Electronics product and at least one Furniture product at any time. List each qualifying customer once, showing customer ID and name.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND p.category = 'Electronics') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND p.category = 'Furniture');

question: Which products have a total quantity sold greater than the average total quantity sold per product? Include all catalog products in the average, treating unsold products as having zero units sold. Show product ID, name, and total quantity sold.
expected_sql: WITH product_sales AS (SELECT p.id, p.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.quantity), 0) AS total_quantity FROM products p LEFT JOIN orders o ON p.id = o.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name) SELECT id, name, total_quantity FROM product_sales WHERE total_quantity > (SELECT AVG(total_quantity) FROM product_sales);

question: Find customers who placed orders in 2024 but none in 2025. Show each qualifying customer once as customer ID followed by name.
expected_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-01-01') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01');
